messages.author: 9f3646dab857d041
messages.subject: stepwiseqtl and refining mqms
parts:
Hi all, and Karl, 

I'm fitting multiple qtl models to an eQTL dataset, looking for additional loci and epistasis (beyond single local/distant effects). 
For the most part, results from stepwiseqtl look pretty sensible and interesting, but I'm getting plenty of screwy results too and am thinking about how best to refine the output. There's ~1/3 or so (of 370 predicted interactions) where the number of individuals is severely imbalanced (often from a case of segregation distortion that effects half of chromosome 1 - I'll drop these markers in future - but many others where very tightly linked qtl are predicted). A couple examples are attached.

What's the best way to deal with these? Usually the main additive effect dominates the interaction so the pLOD is no help, and I don't see any measure of confidence based on the number of individuals. Shouldn't these be penalised in some way during model selection?
If I operate on the qtl object from stepwiseqtl to drop a position (e.g. where confidence intervals overlap) this kills the interaction terms in the formula, so for now I'm just parsing the results and rebuilding from scratch, hard filtering on individual counts. Is there a better way?
As for significance, is it appropriate to use an empirical pLOD threshold generated from permuted data? I'm using initial penalties from scantwo permutations for selection, but I still need to control fdr right?

Finally, should I be looking at other methods in rqtl (mqm - I've had errors due to map expansion after augmentation so haven't pursued this) or elsewhere for assessing hotspots? I've been playing with qtlhot and random forests.

Thanks for your advice,
Luke

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] stepwiseqtl and refining mqms
parts:
I don't have a good solution to this problem, of spurious tightly linked QTL.

I agree that you do need to account for the search across multiple expression traits, but at present I don't have a recommendation about what to do.

karl
